newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Migros 1996 sales fall first time since 1941.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Migros 1996 sales fall first time since 1941.

text.p: The Migros cooperative, Switzerland's largest retail chain, said sales last year fell for the first time since 1941, reflecting the country's sluggish economy and depressed consumer sentiment.

Migros' domestic turnover fell by one percent to 12.9 billion Swiss francs in 1996 and average spending by Migros' 422 million shoppers slipped 1.8 percent to 29.91 francs from 30.45 francs, the cooperative said in a statement.
Including Migros' stores in neighboring France and Germany, Migros' total turnover fell 0.7 percent to 13 billion francs. Prices at Migros eased by one percent on average last year.
"The development of sales corresponds with the economic environment and consumer sentiment," Migros' chief exectuive Peter Everts was quoted as saying.
Overall retail sales in Switzerland also fell last year, but Migros was able to increase its market share, the statement said, without giving futher details.
The number of Migros stores rose slightly to 578 from 573 and the selling space rose 3.7 percent to 915,929 square metres.
